messages:
Priya: Kicking off thread for MercuryBank POC. They require private connectivity from their VPC into our Private deployment, strict source-IP preservation, and inline SNI/TLS inspection on their side. They also asked how this impacts our quoting (monthly infra + egress).

Ben: TL;DR: For source-IP preservation you must host workers inside their VPC (Private deployment) or terminate/load-balance in their network and forward X-Forwarded-For. PrivateLink typically NATs on provider side unless you use NLB TCP passthrough.

Taylor: Adding topology options for NetSec review:
- Pattern 1 (Recommended for audit): Private deployment with agents in customer VPC. Our control plane still runs in our control network but data plane stays in-customer. Pros: preserves client IPs, full mTLS options, no internet egress. Cons: longer onboarding, infra minimums.
- Pattern 2 (Scale-friendly): Transit Gateway + customer-managed egress proxy. Use PrivateLink endpoints to expose services; route via TGW for multi-account. Pros: easier ops across accounts. Cons: if our workers are outside their VPC, you lose native client IP unless proxy forwards headers.
- Pattern 3 (Simple): VPC peering for single-account POC. Quick but not good for many VPCs.

Priya: They asked if SNI inspection is possible when using PrivateLink + NLB. NetSec needs a concise statement we can paste into their questionnaire.

Ben: Short answer: If you configure TCP passthrough on the NLB and terminate TLS at your inline device, SNI is visible. If our service terminates TLS (TLS termination at provider), SNI is consumed and not inspectable downstream. Recommend customer terminates TLS at their proxy and then mTLS to our internal worker.

Taylor: Minimal firewall/egress checklist for customer (to paste into questionnaire):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 from customer worker subnets to our control-plane IP ranges
- Allow inbound from customer subnets to worker ENIs (if private deploy)
- If using PrivateLink: create interface endpoints in their VPC and ensure SG allows TCP 443 to the endpoint
- If using TGW: route tables need propagation to VPC subnets and NACLs permit ephemeral ports 1024-65535 for client responses

NetSec: Can you list the concrete CIDRs for control plane and data plane? We'll need a table for the SOC questionnaire.

Priya: I'll ask infra for CIDRs but in the meantime I'll include this phrasing for the questionnaire: "Redwood offers private deployments where runtime workers are instantiated inside the customer's VPC to satisfy source-IP and no-internet-egress requirements. For customers using PrivateLink proxies or TGW-based routing, customers must host TLS termination or ensure their proxy forwards X-Forwarded-For for client IP preservation."

SalesRep: Pricing note for the commercial team: Private deployment requires a minimum reserved capacity commitment for the POC (one-month equivalent). We can credit egress charges if traffic remains within the customer's network (no public egress). I'll add a line item for engineering onboarding time (estimated 8-16 hours).

Ben: Quick verification commands we'll give them:
- curl --resolve api.redwood.example:443:<endpoint-ip> https://api.redwood.example/health -v  # verify SNI passthrough
- tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w capture.pcap 'tcp port 443'  # capture TLS ClientHello to check SNI

Taylor: I'll assemble a one-page summary + sample SG snippet and a short runbook for their infra team: steps to create interface endpoints, configure TGW routes, and test client-ip preservation. Target to post in this thread within 24h.

OpsBot: Ticket NET-4590 created and assigned to Taylor, Ben. Due: 2 business days.

Priya: Thanks all. Scheduling a 30m handshake with MercuryBank today 15:30 PT to walk through the runbook and confirm their firewall team is available. I'll attach the SOC excerpt and the pricing ballpark.

NetSec: Please ensure the SOC excerpt includes our recommended audit fields: connection timestamps, source IP, threat detections, and retention window.

Taylor: Will do. Draft uploading shortly.

SalesRep: I'll prepare a POC quote PDF with two options (Private deploy + onboarding fee) and (Hosted with egress credit + Proxy pattern). Sending draft to this thread before 15:00.

Priya: Great—meeting invite sent.
